chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about a man who performs ghusl, then finds moisture, while he had urinated before performing ghusl. He said: If he had urinated before performing ghusl, then he does not repeat the ghusl.

key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: the ritual bath required after janabah
key_terms.بَالَ: urinated, serving here as istibrāʾ before ghusl
key_terms.قَبْلَ: before, indicating the sequence relevant to the ruling

ai.seo_question: If someone finds moisture after ghusl from janabah, does he need to repeat the ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity after ghusl from janabah. It states that if a man had urinated before performing ghusl and later finds moisture, he does not need to repeat the ghusl, indicating the legal effect of prior istibrāʾ by urination.
